answer: Latent Anchor Drift Scoring. Each epoch, an agent identity's action graph is hashed into a compact behavioural sketch; the sketch must drift no more than a fixed rate from its prior-epoch anchor. To migrate identity to a new cluster, an attacker must operate it long enough on an umber of low-value tasks to rebuild a matching history. Divergence beyond tolerance quarantines the identity to a fresh island where its influence is capped until consistency is re-earned. Cost: sustained compute and time per identity, scaling linearly with the number of identities held.
